The maintained replication code behind these errata is at <https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/murphy_etal_2026> and is archived at Zenodo at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24168406>, a DOI that always resolves to the latest version.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

archive <- here("maintained", "archive_run", "replication_archive")
slopes <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "corrected_slopes.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
signs <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "sign_audit.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
ads <- read_csv(file.path(archive, "data", "ad_df_emotions.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
exps_clean <- read_rds(file.path(archive, "data", "exps_clean.rds"))
pairwise <- read_rds(file.path(archive, "data", "estimates", "observed_pairwise_frame.rds"))

slope <- function(spec, dv_name, index_name, column = "estimate") {
  hit <- slopes |> filter(specification == spec, dv == dv_name, index == index_name)
  stopifnot(nrow(hit) == 1)
  hit[[column]]
}
label <- function(spec, dv_name, index_name) {
  sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", slope(spec, dv_name, index_name), slope(spec, dv_name, index_name, "std_error"))
}
shift <- function(dv_name, index_name, spec) {
  str_glue("{label('published', dv_name, index_name)} becomes {label(spec, dv_name, index_name)}")
}

# The opening paragraph says no article-figure slope reaches significance under any correction.
figure_rows <- slopes |> filter(index != "rating_index", index != "intended" | dv %in% c("Favorability", "Vote Choice"))
stopifnot(all(figure_rows$p_value > 0.05))

corrected_slope <- slope("sanders", "Favorability", "rating_index")
stopifnot(slope("sanders", "Favorability", "rating_index", "p_value") < 0.05)
two_ad_n <- n_distinct(pairwise$caseid)
two_ad_arm <- read_rds(file.path(archive, "data", "exps.rds")) |> filter(assignment == "Two Ads")
stopifnot(nrow(two_ad_arm) == two_ad_n, n_distinct(two_ad_arm$caseid) == two_ad_n, setequal(two_ad_arm$caseid, pairwise$caseid))
two_ad_compared <- sum(!is.na(pairwise$cate_fav_correct))
stopifnot(!any(map_lgl(two_ad_arm, \(column) sum(!is.na(column)) == 5070)))

# The appendix tables that hold the same rows as entry 1's slope, refit in corrected_slopes.R.
table_cells <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "corrected_favorability_tables.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(part != "footer")
cells_changed <- sum(table_cells$published != table_cells$sanders)
columns_changed <- table_cells |> filter(published != sanders) |> distinct(column) |> pull(column)
stopifnot(setequal(columns_changed, c("Dem (PD)", "Ind (PD)", "Rep (PD)", "All", "All (2)")))
all_star_moves <- table_cells |>
  filter(part == "estimate_cell", str_detect(published, fixed("*")) != str_detect(sanders, fixed("*")))
index_star_moves <- all_star_moves |>
  filter(term == "rating_estimate") |>
  mutate(text = str_glue("{table} {column}, {published} to {sanders}") |> str_replace_all(fixed("*"), "\\*"))
figure_labels <- c(slope("sanders", "Favorability", "negative_index"), slope("sanders", "Favorability", "negative_index", "std_error"),
                   slope("sanders", "Favorability", "positive_index"), slope("sanders", "Favorability", "positive_index", "std_error"),
                   slope("sanders", "Favorability", "intended"), slope("sanders", "Favorability", "intended", "std_error"))

# The accuracy scripts repeat the rescale. Rerun with the line deleted, in corrected_accuracy.R.
accuracy <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "corrected_accuracy.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(str_starts(term, "cate_"))
accuracy_changed <- accuracy |> filter(sprintf("%.3f", estimate_published) != sprintf("%.3f", estimate_corrected))
stopifnot(all(str_starts(accuracy_changed$term, "cate_fav_")))
accuracy_shift <- function(kind_name, term_name) {
  hit <- accuracy |> filter(kind == kind_name, term == term_name)
  stopifnot(nrow(hit) == 1)
  str_glue("{sprintf('%.3f', hit$estimate_published)} becomes {sprintf('%.3f', hit$estimate_corrected)}")
}
overall_individual <- accuracy |> filter(kind == "individual", term %in% c("cate_fav_all_correct_pct_overall", "cate_vote_all_correct_pct_overall"))
stopifnot(all(overall_individual$contains_half_corrected))
democrats_overall <- accuracy |> filter(term == "cate_fav_dem_correct_pct_overall")
stopifnot(nrow(democrats_overall) == 2, !any(democrats_overall$contains_half_published), all(democrats_overall$contains_half_corrected))

# Entry 9: two rows of Table D.16 share a title.
sacrifice <- ads |> filter(ad_title == "Sacrifice")
sacrifice_arms <- exps_clean |> filter(ad_id %in% sacrifice$ad_id) |> count(ad_id, date)
stopifnot(nrow(sacrifice) == 2, n_distinct(sacrifice$ad_sponsor) == 1, n_distinct(sacrifice$emotion_valence) == 1,
          nrow(sacrifice_arms) == 2, n_distinct(sacrifice_arms$date) == 1, n_distinct(sacrifice_arms$n) == 1)
treatments <- nrow(distinct(filter(exps_clean, ad_id != 3), ad_id, date))

primary <- exps_clean |> filter(election_phase == "Primary Election", ad_id != 3) |> distinct(ad_id) |>
  left_join(ads, by = join_by(ad_id), relationship = "one-to-one")
positive_primary <- sum(primary$emotion_valence == "positive")
republican_attacks <- primary |> filter(ad_valence == "Anti Trump", ad_sponsor %in% c("our principles pac", "cruz"))
attack_positive <- ads |> filter(str_detect(ad_valence, "Anti"), emotion_valence == "positive")
stopifnot(nrow(attack_positive) == 3, nrow(republican_attacks) == 3)
titles <- \(d) str_flatten_comma(str_c("“", d$ad_title, "”"), ", and ")
sign_count <- \(d) signs$sign_differs[signs$dv == d]
sign_total <- \(d) signs$estimates[signs$dv == d]
```

```{r entries}
# that changes. A note-form entry corrects nothing, and its corrected field is NA.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  str_glue("`clean_exps.R` applies `(favorBS_rev - 1)/4` twice, so Sanders favorability runs from -0.25 to 0 where the other candidates run from 0 to 1, and the 12 favorability estimates for the two pro-Sanders ads are a quarter of their size. The slope stays significant. The same rows enter Figure 2, where {shift('Favorability', 'negative_index', 'sanders')} and {shift('Favorability', 'positive_index', 'sanders')}, and Figure 3, where {shift('Favorability', 'intended', 'sanders')}. Tables C.1, C.6, C.11, and E.17 hold the same rows, and refitting them changes {cells_changed} of their {nrow(table_cells)} printed coefficients and standard errors, in the {length(columns_changed)} columns that include the Sanders ads. Stars move on {nrow(all_star_moves)} coefficients. On the index coefficient the moves are {str_flatten_comma(index_star_moves$text, ', and ')}. No Figure 2 or 3 slope becomes distinguishable from zero. Both accuracy scripts repeat the same line, and there a CATE's scale can change which ad wins a matchup. Rerunning them without the line changes {nrow(accuracy_changed)} of the {nrow(accuracy)} favorability and vote choice statistics behind Figures E.11 and E.12, all on favorability. In Figure E.11 the overall estimate, {accuracy_shift('individual', 'cate_fav_all_correct_pct_overall')}, and the Democrats' estimate, {accuracy_shift('individual', 'cate_fav_dem_correct_pct_overall')}. In Figure E.12 the overall estimate, {accuracy_shift('group', 'cate_fav_all_correct_pct_overall')}, and the Democrats' estimate, {accuracy_shift('group', 'cate_fav_dem_correct_pct_overall')}. Both Democrats' intervals exclude 0.50 as published and contain it once corrected. The overall individual intervals still contain 0.50, so the appendix's conclusion that individuals are no better than random guessing stands."),

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry),
          all(is.na(entries$corrected) == (entries$form == "note")),
          all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values) == (entries$class == "quantity")))

# Each corrected value must sit inside a marked span of its corrected sentence. A figure label that
# no sentence prints must sit in the entry's note instead, which is entry 1's six label values.
values_in_spans <- function(corrected, values, note) {
  spans <- str_remove_all(str_c(str_extract_all(corrected, "\\[\\[.*?\\]\\]")[[1]], collapse = " "), ",")
  all(str_detect(str_c(spans, " ", note), fixed(str_split(values, ";")[[1]])))
}
quantities <- entries |> filter(class == "quantity")
stopifnot(all(pmap_lgl(list(quantities$corrected, quantities$corrected_values, quantities$note), values_in_spans)),
          all(str_count(quantities$claim_ids, ";") == str_count(quantities$corrected_values, ";")))

english_count <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six")[sum(entries$form == "note")]
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
emit_entry <- function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ", str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ", bold(e$published), sep = "")
  if (e$form != "note") cat("\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), sep = "")
  cat("\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

This note lists corrections and `r english_count` unresolved items in "Do Emotional Ads Persuade? Evidence from Real-Time Campaign Advertising Experiments," published in *Political Communication*, doi [10.1080/10584609.2026.2726266](https://doi.org/10.1080/10584609.2026.2726266). Page numbers are the journal's. **No slope in Figures 2, 3, or 4 becomes distinguishable from zero under any correction here, so the article's central null is unchanged.**

```{r article-entries, results="asis"}
walk(entries$entry, emit_entry)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The spine's vocabularies are closed (cleanup of 2026-11-07): a value outside them is a
# typo, and the edition builders read these columns to shape every entry.
stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof"))
)
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
